policy.meaningOfExperiment: A controlled intervention with a declared record, nuisance controls, analysis and stopping rule. Computational and theorem experiments are used where no physical operator or action yet licenses a laboratory claim.
policy.promotionFirewall: A platform analogy tests the declared mechanism only. It does not establish a universal physical identification or new fundamental law.
policy.estimates: Indicative elapsed-time and staffing bands assume access to the stated platform; they are planning ranges, not quotes or commitments.

experiments.title: Pinned-kernel reachability tournament
experiments.estimate: 2–4 weeks; one proof engineer plus one independent reproducer
experiments.platform: A pinned Lean toolchain and a stratified sample of real declarations, synthetic edge cases and deliberately unreachable constructor trees.
experiments.hypothesis: Kernel elaboration and constructor closure identify a strict reachable image whose failures are stable under harmless presentation changes.
intervention: Vary constructor depth, arity and closure while holding the target type fixed
Blind the analyst to reachable versus adversarial cases
Repeat under pinned transparency and compact-constructor policies
experiments.analysis: Estimate reachable occupancy by stratum, then require every classifier error to reduce to a named missing constructor, environment dependency or timeout class.
experiments.success: A held-out reachability sieve predicts all outcomes and emits checkable witnesses.
experiments.nullValue: Reachability depends materially on undeclared environment state or resource limits.
experiments.stopRule: Stop promotion if two pinned rebuilds disagree on any held-out declaration.

experiments.title: Normalization-orbit stability challenge
experiments.estimate: 4–8 weeks; proof engineer and data engineer
experiments.platform: The same declaration corpus expanded into equivalence families by alpha, beta, zeta, metadata, notation and definitional rewrites.
experiments.hypothesis: A canonical address is constant on declared equivalence orbits while retaining distinctions needed by later detectors.
intervention: Generate 20–100 semantics-preserving variants per declaration
Change normalization policy one rule at a time
Insert non-equivalent near neighbours with matched surface statistics
experiments.analysis: Treat normalization as a quotient experiment: measure false splits within orbits and false merges between orbits with bootstrap intervals by declaration family.
experiments.success: A preregistered policy achieves zero false merges and bounded, explained false splits on held-out families.
experiments.nullValue: No single policy is stable across source-native families.
experiments.stopRule: Retain a multi-chart atlas if global canonicalization requires erasing a detector-relevant distinction.

experiments.title: Blind detector-fibre identification challenge
experiments.estimate: 6–10 weeks; modelling, statistics and domain-review trio
experiments.platform: A benchmark mixing real declaration trees, driven-oscillator records, five-coordinate incidence records and synthetic mechanism pairs with controlled collisions.
experiments.hypothesis: Adaptive detector enrichment separates mechanisms at finite cost, or exposes an exact residual equivalence class.
intervention: Reveal label, role, rooted depth, phase, sideband and intervention channels sequentially
Hold out complete mechanism families rather than random rows
Adversarially search for record-equivalent parameter pairs
experiments.analysis: Plot information gained per marginal cost and certify global injectivity only after interval or adversarial optimization over nuisance parameters.
experiments.success: Every declared pair is separated on held-out interventions or assigned to an explicit quotient class.
experiments.nullValue: A nontrivial model pair remains exactly record-equivalent.
experiments.stopRule: Do not add more detectors when the residual equality is algebraic rather than noise-limited.

experiments.title: Two-port positive-response cone tomography
experiments.estimate: 3–6 months on an existing microwave or transport platform
experiments.platform: A passive two-port microwave network first, followed by a common-sample particle/energy response implementation.
experiments.hypothesis: A source-native 2×2 response remains positive and genuinely rank two over a controlled frequency window.
intervention: Drive each port independently and coherently
Sweep frequency, temperature and relative phase
Change the declared source basis without refitting physics
experiments.analysis: Use covariance-aware cone projection; test whether the smaller eigenvalue remains positive after de-embedding and order-of-limits checks.
experiments.success: The second response direction survives calibration, basis and low-frequency scaling.
experiments.nullValue: Every controlled window becomes rank one or scheme-sheared.
experiments.stopRule: Stop physical interpretation if passivity violations exceed the calibrated systematic envelope.

experiments.title: Reversal-calibrated orientation lift
experiments.estimate: 6–12 months using an integrated-photonic or microwave platform
experiments.platform: A three-mode interferometric loop with an independently calibrated birefringent, chiral or boundary reference axis.
experiments.hypothesis: An oriented phase changes sign under physical reversal while even overlap and attenuation do not.
intervention: Run forward and reversed loops
Flip the external orientation reference
Remove the reference element while preserving the loop
experiments.analysis: Fit even and odd channels jointly; the claimed lift is the interaction term between loop reversal and reference reversal, not a fitted absolute phase.
experiments.success: The odd contrast reverses twice as predicted and is stable to gauge choice.
experiments.nullValue: The signal is removable by basis phase or reproduced by differential loss.
experiments.stopRule: Reject the orientation claim if the reference cannot be calibrated without selected-state data.

experiments.title: Three-mode projector-return, holonomy and oriented-seam transfer
experiments.estimate: 9–18 months including foundry cycle
experiments.platform: Silicon-nitride, microwave or femtosecond-written modes implementing a closed three-mode coupling loop with programmable edge phases, a dark subspace and calibrated directional ports.
experiments.hypothesis: The spectral projector returns after a closed control loop while the coherent frame acquires a nontrivial, order-sensitive holonomy. Independently, the gauge-invariant edge-phase sum survives phase redistribution: resonance poles identify opposite loop orientations, while directional complex transfer distinguishes them. A central -I2 return is tested separately: it is reversal-even, so it must be identified by coherent endpoint-frame comparison and one-loop/two-loop traversal parity.
intervention: Fabricate forward, reverse and path-order-swapped coupling profiles
Inject a tomographically complete input set
Sweep wavelength and deliberately add calibrated splitting and loss
Redistribute phase among the three edges while holding the loop sum fixed
Reverse the loop phase with edge magnitudes and detunings fixed
Execute one and two identical traversals with the same independently calibrated endpoint reference
record: Forward and reverse complex transfer across the full resonance band
Endpoint frame-overlap matrix H=A_final A_initial^T, its centrality residual and sign(tr(H)/2)
controls: Open-loop control showing that an isolated edge phase is basis-removable
Direct-feedthrough injection followed by frozen complex background subtraction
Endpoint-reference recalibration without selected-state data and a static sign-flip/cable-order mimic
experiments.analysis: Blindly compare geometric, static-splitting, reciprocal-network and loss models using held-out wavelengths and reversal data. Require fixed-flux phase redistributions to agree before interpreting the flux-reversal-odd directional record. Analyze the central-return channel separately: require projector closure, H inside a predeclared centrality band around -I2 after one traversal and +I2 after two, and stability under endpoint-reference recalibration.
experiments.success: Projector closure and reversed noncommuting transport survive independent loss calibration; phase redistributions at fixed loop sum agree, opposite loop phases are isospectral and the held-out directional statistic changes sign with its predicted magnitude. If the binary central channel is claimed, the one-loop -I2 and two-loop +I2 endpoint returns must also pass their independent centrality and reference controls.
experiments.nullValue: A static, reciprocal or non-Hermitian nuisance model predicts every record, improving coherent-network calibration while closing the claimed discriminator at the achieved sensitivity.
experiments.stopRule: Do not fabricate until full-wave tolerancing leaves a resolvable process-matrix margin. Stop at an engineering demonstration unless an independent source calculation predicts a continuous loop phase beyond the binary modular sign, coupling ratios or a defect response without fitting them to the device; require replication on a second carrier before a new-physics interpretation.

experiments.title: Selector-on/off basin tomography
experiments.estimate: 9–18 months; can share EX-006 hardware
experiments.platform: The holonomy chip or modular acoustic loop extended by a separately addressable dissipative or anisotropic selector segment Y.
experiments.hypothesis: A carrier-native Y changes the fixed point and contraction tangent rather than merely relabelling a preselected outcome.
intervention: Prepare at least twelve initial states spanning the accessible manifold
Toggle Y on/off and reverse its axis
Match total loss and cycle time across conditions
controls: Y inferred only from independent calibration
experiments.analysis: Fit a common generative return map with Y as a preregistered intervention and compare contraction spectra, not endpoint images alone.
experiments.success: Y produces the predicted fixed-point shift and subunit tangent eigenvalue across initial states.
experiments.nullValue: The same contraction occurs with Y absent or after loss matching.
experiments.stopRule: Stop if Y can only be defined retrospectively from the selected state.

experiments.title: Complete-outcome instrument tomography
experiments.estimate: 6–12 months on a superconducting qutrit or continuously monitored qubit
experiments.platform: A three-level superconducting circuit with single-shot IQ readout, real-time feedback and calibrated missed-record efficiency.
experiments.hypothesis: Apparent attraction can be separated into unconditional channel dynamics and record-conditioned trajectory branches.
intervention: Vary measurement strength and efficiency
Run feedback on/off
Retain every outcome including null and discarded records
experiments.analysis: Reconstruct completely positive outcome maps, sum them to the unconditional channel and propagate efficiency uncertainty.
experiments.success: Conditioned and unconditional maps are separately identifiable and predict held-out sequences.
experiments.nullValue: Only postselected branches contract while the unconditional manifold remains neutral.
experiments.stopRule: No selection claim is admitted if unrecorded outcomes can span the effect.

experiments.title: Matched-contraction stochastic energetics trial
experiments.estimate: 4–8 months on an optical-feedback trap
experiments.platform: A 1–2 μm colloidal bead in a programmable double-well optical or feedback potential.
experiments.hypothesis: Protocols with matched endpoint contraction can have measurably different heat, work, activity and information-reset costs.
intervention: Implement equilibrium relaxation, hidden-cycle drive and measurement-feedback protocols
Match endpoint error and completion time
Sweep protocol duration
experiments.analysis: Infer trajectory-level energetics before comparing equal-precision/equal-speed frontiers; keep controller energy as a separate ledger.
experiments.success: Distinct protocols occupy separated precision-speed-cost surfaces despite equal contraction.
experiments.nullValue: Differences vanish after complete apparatus accounting.
experiments.stopRule: Do not infer cost from convergence rate alone.

experiments.title: Rare-event and hysteresis trajectory campaign
experiments.estimate: 6–12 months; long unattended acquisition required
experiments.platform: An injection-locked VCSEL, Kerr resonator or nanomagnetic element with tunable bistability and single-event readout.
experiments.hypothesis: Waiting-time tails, sweep hysteresis and reversal asymmetry distinguish metastable selection from a unique deterministic attractor.
intervention: Sweep control in both directions at logarithmically spaced rates
Hold inside the bistable region for long dwell windows
Apply calibrated weak perturbation pulses
experiments.analysis: Fit survival curves and large-deviation rate functions jointly; reserve late trajectories for posterior predictive tests.
experiments.success: One mechanistic landscape predicts rates, hysteresis width and perturbation response across sweeps.
experiments.nullValue: Observed memory is detector lag or ordinary bandwidth filtering.
experiments.stopRule: Stop adding dwell time once confidence intervals are dominated by nonstationary drift rather than rare-event count.

experiments.title: Tunable finite-chain pole-to-cut spectrometer
experiments.estimate: 4–9 months with microwave or acoustic resonators
experiments.platform: A 10–40 site coupled-resonator chain with one tunable side-coupled defect and access to both end-port scattering and local density of states.
experiments.hypothesis: Bound states, edge collisions, resonances, phase winding and time delay form one branch-consistent ledger on the same carrier.
intervention: Tune defect frequency and coupling through both certified pole collisions
Repeat for several chain lengths and losses
Excite locally and from both scattering ports
experiments.analysis: Fit a causal rational model globally, continue poles with uncertainty and compare the finite-band Levinson ledger before extrapolating length.
experiments.success: Every spectral stratum and both collision laws agree without changing the model family.
experiments.nullValue: Crossings depend on sampling, fit order or Riemann-sheet convention.
experiments.stopRule: Freeze the result at the finite carrier if loss prevents stable continuation.

experiments.title: Same-film tensor-to-Casimir closure
experiments.estimate: 18–36 months across materials, transport, optics and force metrology teams
experiments.platform: One batch of anisotropic magnetic films split into witness coupons and a force/torque device, with common growth and metrology records.
experiments.hypothesis: Broadband causal response inferred without force data predicts a differential Casimir force or torque after all ordinary nuisances are propagated.
intervention: Measure Hall, Seebeck, Nernst and magneto-optical response versus temperature, field and angle
Freeze a causal tensor posterior
Measure angle- and distance-dependent parallel-minus-antiparallel force/torque
controls: Blind force analysis and dummy spacing scans
experiments.analysis: Propagate the pre-force tensor posterior through Lifshitz theory with a full nuisance covariance; prohibit response refitting to force data.
experiments.success: The preregistered differential curve is recovered with nuisance alternatives disfavoured.
experiments.nullValue: Optical-tail, patch, roughness or magnetic freedom spans the effect.
experiments.stopRule: Do not proceed to force fabrication until OT-006 cross-channel prediction passes on held-out films.

experiments.boundaryType: rank surface and order of limits
experiments.title: Common-sample multichannel Onsager-rank experiment
experiments.estimate: 12–24 months including microfabrication
experiments.platform: A suspended four-terminal microbridge allowing independent electrical and thermal biases, magnetic-field reversal and AC thermometry.
experiments.hypothesis: The particle/energy response has a stable second eigen-direction in a declared low-frequency transport window.
intervention: Independently modulate voltage and heater power
Sweep frequency, temperature, field, filling and contact geometry
Reverse injection/emission contacts
experiments.analysis: Infer eigenvalues with errors in both currents and forces; test limit ordering and compare with common-sample KPM/typicality.
experiments.success: Rank two and reciprocity survive frequency-window, size and energy-gauge changes.
experiments.nullValue: The second direction is contact leakage or exits every controlled low-frequency window.
experiments.stopRule: Stop rank claims when thermal cross-talk exceeds the smaller singular value.

experiments.title: Defect information beyond mode count
experiments.estimate: 6–12 months with acoustic or topoelectric resonator arrays
experiments.platform: A reconfigurable 2D acoustic or circuit lattice containing matched trivial, domain-wall, partial-dislocation and threefold-quotient defects.
experiments.hypothesis: Defects with the same protected mode count remain distinguishable by oriented transport, spatial texture and scattering phase.
intervention: Move source and detector around the defect
Reverse helicity or circulation
Add controlled symmetry-preserving and symmetry-breaking disorder
experiments.analysis: Condition on equal index and compare the remaining response tensor; demand a held-out observable beyond mode count.
experiments.success: A non-index record robustly tracks defect geometry and quotient operation.
experiments.nullValue: All extra information is arbitrary boundary data.
experiments.stopRule: Retain only the topological count if disorder destroys the extra record before the bulk gap closes.

experiments.title: Disorder–spread–coarse-graining scaling tube
experiments.estimate: 6–12 months on a programmable resonator or qubit array
experiments.platform: Arrays of 16–128 microwave/acoustic resonators or available quantum-simulator sites with programmable onsite disorder and couplings.
experiments.hypothesis: A small set of propagation and memory invariants remains stable across disorder, size, time and coarse-graining.
intervention: Quench a local excitation
Sweep disorder distribution and correlation length
Repeat across array sizes and detector aggregation scales
experiments.analysis: Fit a joint finite-size/time scaling model and test semigroup consistency between raw and coarse observations.
experiments.success: One invariant scaling tube predicts held-out size and disorder ensembles.
experiments.nullValue: Every apparent bound is detector- or size-specific.
experiments.stopRule: Do not extrapolate if fitted constants drift monotonically with the largest available size.

experiments.title: Code-island operator-law falsification
experiments.estimate: 2–6 months; algebra, coding and proof expertise
experiments.platform: The finite Monster-address, Golay/Leech-neighbour and 24-dimensional form data already represented in the corpus.
experiments.hypothesis: At least one source-derived operator family—not labels alone—satisfies preregistered Hecke, modular-trace or product-preserving relations.
intervention: Define operators before inspecting occupancy coincidences
Apply them to the full finite atlas
Compare integral, rational and mod-p reductions
controls: Same divisor multiset with destroyed multiplication
experiments.analysis: Require exact identities over integers or declared rings; numerical near-equality has no evidential weight.
experiments.success: A nontrivial operator law holds without fitting prime-address occupancy.
experiments.nullValue: Only numerology, dimensions or divisor labels survive.
experiments.stopRule: Close the branch after all natural source-derived multiplications fail the preregistered identities.

experiments.title: Two-carrier commuting-square hardware-in-the-loop test
experiments.estimate: 12–24 months after a source-native map is written
experiments.platform: A photonic three-mode chip and an acoustic or microwave three-port emulator implementing the same declared A2 operation in native units.
experiments.hypothesis: A provenance-bearing transformation transports projector, complex structure, losses and observable records between carriers while preserving composition.
intervention: Prepare matched labelled states in both carriers
Apply generators singly and in compositions
Transport predictions in both directions without basis refitting
experiments.analysis: Test path equality in the commuting square on held-out states, with separate structural and calibrated physical error budgets.
experiments.success: Both paths agree and the map predicts a native observable in the second carrier.
experiments.nullValue: Agreement exists only after erasing labels, units or orientation.
experiments.stopRule: Do not build the second device until the source-side map preserves products symbolically.

experiments.title: Uniform-limit adversarial scattering benchmark
experiments.estimate: 6–18 months depending on whether a theorem survives
experiments.platform: Families of finite chains, lattice gauge Hamiltonians and D4 defect operators with controllable volume, regulator, time and observable class.
experiments.hypothesis: A proposed positivity, gap or admissibility bound has constants uniform in every declared limiting direction.
intervention: Search adversarial sequences jointly over volume, regulator and boundary condition
Enlarge the observable class
Compare pole, phase, Euclidean and real-time estimators
experiments.analysis: Attempt to falsify uniformity first; a successful result must supply explicit constants and domain assumptions.
experiments.success: One bound remains positive and stable under all declared limits.
experiments.nullValue: An admissible sequence drives the bound to zero or changes its sign.
experiments.stopRule: Record a scoped no-go once a countersequence is certified; do not replace it with larger finite numerics.

experiments.title: Joined torsion–flavour–cosmology likelihood with a polarized null experiment
experiments.estimate: 12–36 months after a frozen action and matching packet exist
experiments.platform: A rotating unpolarized source mass near a K–Rb–Ne comagnetometer or polarized spin sensor, joined to collider/flavour and cosmological public likelihoods through one action.
experiments.hypothesis: One protected parameter map predicts range, species ratios and signs across laboratory, flavour and cosmological observables.
intervention: Modulate source distance, velocity and orientation
Reverse sensor polarization and source rotation
Freeze threshold matching before opening laboratory data
experiments.analysis: Perform one hierarchical likelihood with shared parameters and explicit theory errors; report the generic-EFT fit beside the protected model.
experiments.success: A common no-refit parameter point survives all channels and predicts a held-out reversal or range curve.
experiments.nullValue: Generic free pseudoscalar coefficients fit equally well or one dataset requires an incompatible parameter value.
experiments.stopRule: No apparatus-specific interpretation begins until the action fixes the measured operator and species ratios.

experiments.title: Exceptional-model end-to-end red-team
experiments.estimate: 12–36 months for one fully specified candidate
experiments.platform: A symbolic and numerical pipeline accepting one exceptional-group action, representation dictionary, vacuum and symmetry-breaking chain.
experiments.hypothesis: A single candidate can pass anomaly, Hessian, gauge-spectrum, threshold and observable gates without freely chosen embeddings.
intervention: Enumerate the full chiral spectrum and anomaly polynomial
Compute the complete scalar Hessian and gauge masses including coloured directions
Run RG and threshold matching to a frozen low-energy likelihood
record: Running couplings and held-out observable predictions
experiments.analysis: Use a sequential gate: failure at any exact consistency stage prevents phenomenological fitting; successful candidates are compared by predictive compression.
experiments.success: One anomaly-free stable vacuum produces a no-refit low-energy prediction that beats the independent EFT.
experiments.nullValue: The construction relies on dimension matches, arbitrary embeddings or compensating free parameters.
experiments.stopRule: Terminate a candidate immediately on anomaly, ghost, unstable coloured direction or underdetermined matching.
